newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil signs another state debt refinancing deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil signs another state debt refinancing deal.

text.p: The Brazilian government Thursday signed a 729 million real debt refinancing deal with the state of Mato Grosso, Finance Ministry officials said.
The officials said Finance Minister Pedro Malan signed the agreement in Brasilia with Mato Grosso governor Dante de Oliveira.
The refinancing deal is the latest in a series of agreements Brasilia has struck with the states in a bid to sort out their chaotic finances and ensure they start repaying their debts.
Mato Grosso's debt maturity will be lengthened to 30 years and it will pay 6.0 percent a year, adjusted for inflation. In return, the state must retire 20 percent of its debt through asset sales.
Mato Grosso's total debt is 3.4 billion reais. The rest had already been refinanced under a previous agreement.
On Wednesday, Malan signed a similar deal with Rio de Janeiro state. But because the state could only offer 10 percent of its debt in assets, it is paying 7.5 percent a year interest.
The federal government has signed refinancing deals with Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul states.
